Draw fitted values from the posterior distribution

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/posterior-samples.R
fitted_samples.Rd

Distribution parameters or expected responses drawn from the posterior distribution of a fitted model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
fitted_samples(model, ...)

fitted_samples(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
fitted_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  scale = c("response", "linear_predictor"),
  family_index = NULL,
  quantity = c("parameters", "expectation")
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
fitted_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  scale = c("response", "linear_predictor"),
  quantity = c("parameters", "expectation")
)

Arguments

model

a fitted model of the supported types; see diagnostic_support.

...

arguments passed to other methods. For fitted_samples(), these are passed on to mgcv::predict.gam(). For posterior_samples() these are passed on to fitted_samples(). For predicted_samples() these are passed on to the relevant simulate() method.

data

data frame; new observations at which the posterior draws from the model should be evaluated. If not supplied, the data used to fit the model will be used for data, if available in model.

n_draws

positive integer; total retained draws across all chains. Required when generating draws. With method = "user", the supplied matrix determines the count; an explicit count must agree with its rows.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

seed

numeric; a random seed for the simulations.

method

character; which method should be used to draw samples from the posterior distribution. "gaussian" uses a Gaussian (Laplace) approximation to the posterior. "mh" uses a Metropolis Hastings sampler that alternates t proposals with proposals based on a shrunken version of the posterior covariance matrix. "inla" uses a variant of Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation due to Wood (2019), (currently not implemented). "user" allows for user-supplied posterior draws as a coefficient matrix.

n_cores

positive integer; maximum concurrent MH chains using mirai, capped at chains. Existing workers are reused; otherwise temporary workers are created and cleaned up. Only used by method = "mh".

n_threads

positive integer; threads within Gaussian sampling using mvnfast. Defaults to one. This is separate from concurrent MH chains.

burnin

numeric; number of samples to discard as the burnin draws. Only used with method = "mh".

thin

positive integer; retain every thin iterations after burn-in.

t_df

numeric; degrees of freedom for t distribution proposals. Only used with method = "mh".

rw_scale

numeric; Factor by which to scale posterior covariance matrix when generating random walk proposals. Negative or non finite to skip the random walk step. Only used with method = "mh".

frequentist

logical; TRUE to use the frequentist covariance matrix of the parameter estimators, FALSE to use the Bayesian posterior covariance matrix of the parameters.

unconditional

logical; if TRUE (and frequentist == FALSE) then the Bayesian smoothing parameter uncertainty corrected covariance matrix is used, if available.

draws

matrix; user supplied posterior draws to be used when method = "user".

diagnostics

logical; calculate coefficient R-hat, effective sample sizes, and Monte Carlo standard errors using the optional posterior package.

mh_backend

character; "mgcv" preserves mgcv::gam.mh(). "gratia" uses compiled common-family likelihoods. "family" uses a compiled MH loop with callbacks to the fitted family object. Both support independent-observation bam fits. Smoothing parameters and parameters outside the fitted coefficient vector remain fixed. LSS scale and shape coefficients are sampled jointly with location. The family backend caches a full design matrix, smoothing penalty, and proposal factorisation once for all chains.

mvn_method

character; one of "mvnfast" or "mgcv". The default is uses mvnfast::rmvn(), which can be considerably faster at generate large numbers of MVN random values than mgcv::rmvn(), but which might not work for some marginal fits, such as those where the covariance matrix is close to singular.

block_size

positive integer; maximum observation rows per block in the gratia MH evaluator. Large designs are evaluated without storing a full matrix.

dense_limit

numeric; maximum number of design-matrix elements to cache for the gratia MH backend. Use zero to force blockwise evaluation.

scale

character; "response" returns natural distribution parameters; "link", "linear_predictor" and "linear predictor" return their predictors. Expectations require "response".

family_index

numeric; optional family-list positions for grouped family (mgcv::gfam()) response predictions, with one integer per requested row. By default membership is recovered from the response/index expression in data, or the fitted membership when data is omitted. This is useful when predicting without responses or with a complex response expression. An explicit index must agree with membership recoverable from data.

quantity

character; "parameters" (the default) returns all distribution parameters represented by predictors, including intercept-only predictors. "expectation" returns the expected response, using every parameter on which it depends, on the response scale only.

Value

A tibble (data frame) in long format, with columns:

  • .row: row of the evaluation data;

  • .draw: globally unique draw identifier;

  • .parameter: the distribution parameter name, or "expectation";

  • .fitted: the parameter, predictor or expected response requested. Multiple-chain output also includes .chain and .iteration. Attached coefficient diagnostics are available through sampling_diagnostics().

Details

Parameter names and definitions are available through family_parameters(). Gaussian LSS returns mean and sd, GEV returns location, scale and shape, and sinh-arcsinh returns location, scale, skewness and tailweight. These shape parameters are not response moments. Natural parameters can differ from native mgcv predictions and inv_link() values. Every parameter in one draw uses the same joint coefficient draw. Global parameters outside the coefficient vector remain fixed and are described in the metadata, rather than returned as fitted parameters.

Use quantity = "expectation" for expected responses labelled "expectation". This includes Gumbel, GEV and sinh-arcsinh mean adjustments and the zero-truncated Poisson adjustment in ziplss(). A GEV expectation does not exist at shape >= 1; parameter and response draws remain available. Categorical expectations are category probabilities, not numeric category scores. .category identifies categories, and .y identifies multivariate responses. Multinomial link output includes a zero reference predictor. Ordinal parameter output is the latent location predictor; its thresholds are global parameters.

The prediction_info attribute records the quantity, scale and resolved parameter descriptions. Unlike posterior_samples(), these draws add no response noise. predicted_samples() instead simulates observations with coefficients held at their fitted values.

For grouped families, coefficient draws preserve the joint model covariance; each row is then transformed using its own fitted component family. Explicit prediction data must identify each row's family: no training-order fallback is used. A two-column response matrix supplies its second column; a numeric column named for the response supplies indices directly. For a response such as cbind(y, index), the index expression can be supplied without y. Missing indices behave like missing required predictors. Link-scale draws do not require family membership.

Grouped parameter output includes the latent location for ordinal components. Grouped expectations include scalar fitted means and ordinal category probabilities, with .category identifying the ordinal category and NA for scalar components. Distributional nuisance parameters are held at their fitted values. This does not add support for general/location-scale families that gfam() itself rejects, nor repair upstream fitting failures (including fixed-theta negative-binomial components and some ziP() fits in some mgcv versions).

Observation rows use the same missing-value convention as posterior_samples(): default results restore na.exclude observations in every draw, while explicit data are evaluated in their own row order.

Note

With data = NULL, fitting offsets are retained, including offsets supplied through the fitting function's offset argument. Explicit prediction data follow mgcv::predict.gam(): offsets in formulas are evaluated from the prediction data, while offsets supplied through the fitting function's offset argument are not transferred to new observations. Include offsets in the formula when predicting at new data; the required offset variables must then be present in data.

References

Wood, S.N., (2020). Simplified integrated nested Laplace approximation. Biometrika 107, 223–230. doi:10.1093/biomet/asz044

Examples

load_mgcv()
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 1000, dist = "normal", scale = 2, seed = 2)
m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat, method = "REML")

fs <- fitted_samples(m1, n_draws = 5, seed = 42)
# \donttest{
fs
#> # A tibble: 5,000 x 4
#>     .row .draw .parameter .fitted
#>    <int> <int> <chr>        <dbl>
#>  1     1     1 mean          6.34
#>  2     2     1 mean          5.08
#>  3     3     1 mean          6.84
#>  4     4     1 mean          7.71
#>  5     5     1 mean          9.23
#>  6     6     1 mean          8.03
#>  7     7     1 mean          6.19
#>  8     8     1 mean          7.28
#>  9     9     1 mean         14.0 
#> 10    10     1 mean         12.7 
#> # i 4,990 more rows
# }

# can generate own set of draws and use them
drws <- generate_draws(m1, n_draws = 2, seed = 24)
fs2 <- fitted_samples(m1, method = "user", draws = drws)
# \donttest{
fs2
#> # A tibble: 2,000 x 4
#>     .row .draw .parameter .fitted
#>    <int> <int> <chr>        <dbl>
#>  1     1     1 mean          6.30
#>  2     2     1 mean          5.12
#>  3     3     1 mean          7.40
#>  4     4     1 mean          7.42
#>  5     5     1 mean          9.40
#>  6     6     1 mean          8.04
#>  7     7     1 mean          5.83
#>  8     8     1 mean          7.30
#>  9     9     1 mean         14.3 
#> 10    10     1 mean         13.1 
#> # i 1,990 more rows
# }
